scope.applicability: Observed on the retained MIN 6000TL-XH installation only.

observation.source: staging Home Assistant HIL log and the corresponding HA TOU test record
observation.transport: Modbus/TCP through the Growatt broker, unit 1

controlled_action.purpose: Change and restore the end word of disabled TOU period 2 without changing its priority or enabled bit

readback.result: Both the changed and restored values matched the requested words after the staging integration's broker-cache delay.

observed: FC16 can update the two-word TOU period pair at H3040-H3041 on this device.
Changing H3041 while H3040 remains disabled preserves the disabled state; the restoration returns H3041 to its original 19:58 value.
not_established: This test does not establish persistence across reboot or a universal write contract for every TL-XH firmware revision.
The test does not validate any production or non-TOU control register.

evidence_assessment.method: controlled hardware-in-the-loop FC16 write, acknowledgement and delayed readback

limitations: The original local log is not redistributed; the retained PDU values are a bounded public-safe extraction.

The local log also contains delayed/stale transaction-id messages while the broker and HA polling overlapped. The final readback result is retained from the test record and should not be interpreted as a transport-latency measurement.
The broker cache workaround used an approximately 11-second wait. The proper broker-side read-after-write refresh remains a separate roadmap item.
